# tte-01 — Mistakes Every Korea Tourist Makes (Framework A · South Korea · human · iteration 1)

Evelyn's first post, and the first Korea pack in the repo, so nothing here is a reuse of an earlier
country pack. Verbatim-vs-drafted and every unverified number are below.

## Verbatim (do not edit)

- **Slide 4 plug** = `CREATIVE.md` Framework A **Plug A**, word for word, with only the
  `DESIGN.md` v3 on-slide transforms applied (sentence-final periods dropped, brand written
  `HOLICAY.COM`, one paragraph per grammar unit). The lowercase and "(you should try it with this
  tiktok 😉)" are the voice and stay untouched. The **caption** carries the same plug fully verbatim,
  periods and `holicay.com` included.
- **Slide 10** title `SAVE THIS` / subtitle `just incase you need it ❤️` (the misspelling is the voice).
- **Hook** = `CREATIVE.md` A title option 3. The subtitle is the doc's "I made all of them on my first
  trip. Don't be me. 😅" compressed to one line without sentence-final periods, per the
  `DESIGN.md` slide-copy rule. Caption line 1 carries the title verbatim.

## Drafted (my copy, fact-checked below)

All seven ❌/✅ body slides. Angles chosen for resonance-first ordering: the famous landmark on slide 2,
the airport (every trip starts there) on slide 3, then the maps/transit/shopping beats, with the
Bukchon curfew and the Seoul-only trap as the deeper cuts.

## Fact-check — verified against a primary or official source

| Claim | Slide | Verified |
|---|---|---|
| Gyeongbokgung is closed every Tuesday | 2 | Yes. Seoul Metropolitan Government + the Royal Palaces official hours page. |
| Adult admission 3,000 won | 2 | Yes. Same sources (19 to 64; 1,500 youth). |
| Free admission when wearing hanbok | 2 | Yes. Same sources. See caveat below. |
| Incheon to central Seoul taxi 55,000 to 100,000 won, 60 to 90 min | 3 | Yes, as a **range**. Sources cluster at 55,000 to 80,000 and 70,000 to 100,000; the slide states the full span so it is true either way. |
| AREX Express, 43 min nonstop from T1 to Seoul Station | 3 | Yes, consistent across every source. |
| Korea restricts export of high-precision map data, so Google Maps walking/driving routing is crippled | 5 | Yes. Act on National Spatial Data Infrastructure / Spatial Data Management Act; behaviour corroborated widely. |
| Naver Map has an English mode and full door-to-door routing | 5 | Yes. |
| Single-journey subway tickets carry a 500 won deposit reclaimed at a refund machine | 6 | Yes. |
| T-money is cheaper per ride than a single-journey ticket and works on buses, taxis and convenience stores | 6 | Yes. |
| Olive Young deducts the tax at the register on a passport | 7 | Yes. Olive Young was the first Korean drugstore to run in-store instant refund; flagship branches (Myeongdong Town, Gangnam) do it at the till. |
| Bukchon red zones are tourist-restricted to 10am to 5pm | 8 | Yes. Korea Times, Feb 2026, after the July 2025 pilot. |
| 100,000 won fine outside those hours | 8 | Yes, reported consistently for individual visitors. See caveat below. |
| KTX Seoul to Busan about 2h30, around 60,000 won standard | 9 | Yes. Standard economy 59,800 won; run times 2h08 to 2h45 depending on stops, so "about 2h30" is a fair middle. |

## Unverified / caveats for the human

1. **Hanbok free entry has clothing rules.** The palace requires the outfit to actually qualify as
   hanbok (correct components, not a costume mashup). Rental shops by the gate know the rule, but the
   slide states the policy without the caveat because the line has no room. Low risk; the caption does
   not overstate it either.
2. **AREX Express fare is deliberately not quoted.** Sources disagree (9,500 / 11,000 / 13,000 won),
   and the AREX customer site would not resolve for a primary check. The slide says "a fraction of the
   fare" and the caption says "a small fraction of the taxi", both true under every reported figure.
   If you want a number on the slide, confirm it at `airportrailroad.com` first.
3. **Bukchon fine amount and scope.** 100,000 won for individuals is widely reported; the Korea Times
   piece I could fetch documents the same 10am to 5pm red-zone window but quotes the separate
   300,000 won penalty for oversized tour buses. Treat the exact individual figure as reported rather
   than confirmed from a Jongno-gu ordinance.
4. **Olive Young instant-refund minimum.** Sources split between a 15,000 won and a 30,000 won minimum
   per receipt, so no threshold appears in the copy. Only the mechanism (passport at the till, tax
   comes off) is claimed, which is not in dispute.
5. **Seoul subway base fare not quoted.** Sources report both 1,400 and 1,550 won for 2026. The slide
   only claims T-money is cheaper per ride than a single-journey ticket, which holds at either fare.
6. **Bukchon closes to tourists daily at 5pm**, but I could not confirm from an official source whether
   Sundays carry an additional full-day restriction. The copy says "after 5pm", which is safe.
